items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had people like Freddy Hubbard and Jackie McLean. We collected money and we paid them whatever.

ctx.x: Ok. So once again... So the Jazz Showcase was really more of - in the beginning days - was more of a presenting organization than looking at actually finding a location that would be a permanent home.

I derived the name from my initials of course, JS and jam sessions, and Jazz Showcase. So as I said we did the Gate of Horn, then we started doing stuff up on Rush Street, different places. And then on Wells Street when the hippie era was going in the sixties. We had a place at Mother Blues, at the Old Town Gate, at the Club Nickel, and I used to do off-night sessions there also. A place called The Window, I had people like Freddy Hubbard and Jackie McLean. We collected money and we paid them whatever. If there…
So how did you support yourself then?
